title: UP BOARD CLASS 4 — English | Creative Writing
description: Subject-wise test on Creative Writing (English) for UP BOARD CLASS 4. 18Q.
subject: upbo4-english

questions.question: Which of these is most important when you want to create a new story from your imagination?

options.text: Copying a story from a book
Using your imagination to think of new ideas
Counting the words in a story

questions.explanation: Creative writing begins with using your own imagination to invent new ideas, characters, and situations.
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question: Which of the following describes a complete sentence?

options.text: A group of words without a full stop.
A group of words that makes complete sense.
options.explanation: A sentence is a group of words that expresses a complete thought and makes sense. It usually starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop, question mark, or exclamation mark.

options.text: Only words that start with a capital letter.

questions.explanation: A sentence is a group of words that expresses a complete thought and makes sense. It usually starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop, question mark, or exclamation mark.
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question: What is the correct way to start a sentence when you are writing?
questions.explanation: All sentences in English begin with a capital letter.
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question: Which of these sentences is written in the correct order to make sense?
questions.explanation: The words "The rabbit ran fast." are arranged in the correct subject-verb-object order, making it a meaningful sentence.
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question: When you want to describe a "beautiful" flower, which type of word are you using?
questions.explanation: An adjective is a word that describes a noun (like 'flower'), telling us more about its quality or characteristic.
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question: A good story should have a beginning, a middle, and what else?
questions.explanation: Every complete story needs a beginning to introduce characters and setting, a middle where the main events happen, and an end to conclude the story.
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question:
Arrange these parts to make a short, logical story:
1. He ate a delicious apple.
2. Rohit went to the market.
3. He bought a red apple.
questions.explanation: First, Rohit went to the market (2), then he bought an apple (3), and finally, he ate it (1).
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question: Which word best completes the sentence to make it more descriptive? "The _____ sun shone brightly in the sky."
questions.explanation: 'Golden' is a descriptive adjective that beautifully captures the colour and warmth of the sun, making the sentence more vivid.
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question: If you are writing a paragraph about "My Favourite Toy," what is the most important information to include?

options.text: The names of your family members.
Details about what your toy looks like and why you like it.
A list of all your favourite foods.
What you want to be when you grow up.

questions.explanation: A paragraph about "My Favourite Toy" should focus on describing the toy itself and your personal connection to it.
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question: Imagine you are describing a happy little puppy. Which sentence best shows its happiness?

options.text: The puppy barked loudly at the cat.
The puppy wagged its tail and licked my hand.
The puppy ate its food quickly.

questions.explanation: Wagging its tail and licking hands are common actions of a happy puppy, best conveying its joyful emotion.
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Using descriptive words like "huge" or "sparkling" makes a story more interesting.
Reason (R): These words help the reader imagine the characters and setting clearly.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.explanation: Descriptive words (adjectives and adverbs) add detail and colour to writing, which indeed helps readers visualize and understand the story better. So, the reason correctly explains the assertion.
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question: You are writing a story about a brave knight. You want to describe his shield. Which sentence would make his shield sound strong and impressive?

options.text: The knight held a plain, old shield.
His shield was small and broken.
He carried a shining, silver shield with a lion's emblem.
The shield was made of wood and paint.

questions.explanation: "Shining, silver" and "lion's emblem" are strong, impressive descriptions that fit a brave knight's shield, conveying strength and importance.
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question: What kind of words do we use to make our writing more interesting by telling us about colours, sizes, and feelings?
questions.explanation: Descriptive words (adjectives) add details and make writing more vivid and engaging by describing how things look, feel, or taste.
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question: Which of these is usually the first part you write in a friendly letter, after the date and address?

options.explanation: In a friendly letter, after the optional address and date, the greeting is the initial way you address the recipient directly.

options.text: The main body of the letter

questions.explanation: In a friendly letter, after the optional address and date, the greeting is the initial way you address the recipient directly.
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question: What is the most important thing a story must have to be complete?

options.text: A beginning, a middle, and an end

questions.explanation: A complete story always has three main parts: how it starts (beginning), what happens (middle), and how it finishes (end).
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question:
Rearrange the following words to form a meaningful sentence:
"is / a / This / big / tree."
questions.explanation: The correct grammatical order for a simple declarative sentence in English is Subject-Verb-Object/Complement. "This is a big tree" follows this structure, making it a clear and meaningful sentence.
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question: When you start writing a creative story, what is the very first thing you should usually think about?

options.text: The characters and what they will do

questions.explanation: Before writing, it's essential to imagine who the story is about (characters) and what happens to them (plot/actions) to build the narrative.
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question: What makes a sentence complete and easy to understand?

options.text: A group of words that makes complete sense
Only a noun and a verb

questions.explanation: A complete sentence expresses a full thought and is understandable on its own. It typically contains a subject and a predicate (verb and its objects/complements).
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question: To describe a cloud that looks like cotton, which word would you use?
questions.explanation: 'Soft' best describes the texture of a fluffy, cotton-like cloud, which is a common descriptive element in creative writing.
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question: Complete the sentence creatively: The little bird sang a ______ song.
questions.explanation: 'Pretty' adds a pleasant and imaginative quality to the bird's song, fitting for creative writing. While other options are possible, 'pretty' is often associated with a pleasing sound.
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question: When you write about what you *imagine* or make up, you are doing:
questions.explanation: Creative writing involves using imagination to make up stories, poems, or descriptions, unlike factual writing or reporting which focuses on real events or information.
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question: Which of these sentences is the *most descriptive* about a cat?

options.text: The cat sat on the mat.

questions.explanation: This sentence uses two descriptive words, 'fluffy' and 'softly', to give a more vivid picture of the cat and its action, making it the most descriptive option.
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question:
Arrange the words to form the most descriptive sentence:
(A) little (B) sparkled (C) river (D) under (E) the (F) sun

options.text: The little river sparkled under the sun.
River little sparkled the sun under.
Under the sun, the little river sparkled.
Sparkled the little river under the sun.

questions.explanation: This option arranges the words into a grammatically correct and descriptive sentence that flows naturally and paints a clear picture.
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question: You want to describe a shy rabbit. Which phrase would you use to show its shyness?

options.text: The rabbit hid behind a bush.
The rabbit ate a carrot loudly.

questions.explanation: Hiding behind a bush suggests shyness or timidity, which is a creative way to show the rabbit's personality rather than just stating it directly.
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question: A story begins: "Once upon a time, a tiny fairy lived in a mushroom house." Which sentence would *best* continue this creative story?

options.text: She loved to play with butterflies.

questions.explanation: This sentence adds a creative and imaginative detail about the fairy's life, continuing the magical theme of the story's beginning.
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question: Which of these sentences uses vivid descriptive words to paint a clear picture?

options.text: The tiny mouse scurried across the floor.

questions.explanation: "Tiny" and "scurried" are vivid descriptive words that help the reader imagine the mouse's size and movement more clearly than simple adjectives or adverbs like "fast" or "red."
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question:
**Assertion (A):** It is important to use descriptive words like 'sparkling' or 'gigantic' in creative writing.
**Reason (R):** Descriptive words make your writing more interesting and help the reader imagine things clearly.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.explanation: The assertion that descriptive words are important in creative writing is true, and the reason provided (they make writing interesting and aid imagination) is precisely why they are important.
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question: Which of the following describes a 'setting' in a story?

options.text: The main person in the story
The place and time where the story happens
The problem that the characters face
The message the story wants to give

questions.explanation: In creative writing, the 'setting' refers to where (place) and when (time) the story takes place.
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question: What is the main purpose of creative writing?

options.text: To write factual reports and news.
To tell stories, poems, or express imagination.
To write school notices and announcements.

questions.explanation: Creative writing focuses on using imagination to create stories, poems, or other expressive pieces, rather than reporting facts or writing formal communications.
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question: Which of these is the most important part to start a creative story?
questions.explanation: A story needs someone or something to be about (character) and a place where it happens (setting) to begin.
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question: What is the first step you should usually take when you want to write a creative story?

options.text: Think about the characters and what will happen in the story.
Write the ending of the story.

questions.explanation: Before writing, it's important to plan your ideas, including characters and plot, to give your story direction.
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question: What is the main purpose of creative writing?

options.text: To give facts and information only.
To write down rules and instructions.
To express ideas, imagination, and feelings freely.

questions.explanation: Creative writing focuses on using imagination and expressing thoughts and emotions, not just presenting facts or rules.
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question: Which punctuation mark should always be placed at the end of a simple statement or sentence?

options.explanation: Question marks are used at the end of questions.
Exclamation marks are used to show strong feelings or emphasis.
A full stop (.) is used to mark the end of a declarative sentence or statement.
Commas are used for pauses within a sentence, not at its end.

questions.explanation: A full stop (.) is used to mark the end of a declarative sentence or statement. Question marks are for questions, exclamation marks for strong feelings, and commas for pauses within a sentence.
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question: Every sentence in a creative paragraph must begin with a ________ and end with a proper punctuation mark.

options.explanation: Sentences do not begin with a small letter.
Every sentence must start with a capital letter.
A comma is not used to start a sentence.
Sentences generally do not start with a number in this context.

questions.explanation: In English writing, every sentence must start with a capital letter and conclude with a suitable end mark, such as a full stop, question mark, or exclamation mark.
questions.hint: Think about the first letter of a sentence.
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question:
Arrange the following sentences in the correct order to make a meaningful story:
1. An apple fell on the ground.
2. Rohan was walking under an apple tree.
3. He picked it up and ate it happily.

options.explanation: The apple cannot fall before Rohan is under the tree.
He cannot eat the apple before it falls.
This is the logical sequence: walking, apple falls, then eating.
He cannot pick up and eat the apple before it falls.

questions.explanation: The logical flow of events is: first, Rohan was walking under the tree (2); next, an apple fell (1); and finally, he picked it up and ate it (3).
questions.hint: What happens first? What happens last?
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question: In an application to your school Principal requesting two days of leave, which is the most suitable greeting (salutation) to use?

options.explanation: This is the standard formal salutation for addressing a Principal.
This is informal and not suitable for an official application.
This is too casual and disrespectful for a formal letter.
This is not a standard or professional form of address.

questions.explanation: An application to a Principal is formal writing, so respectful and polite greetings like 'Respected Sir / Madam' must be used.
questions.hint: Think about the level of formality required when writing to a school authority.
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question: Read the short paragraph written by Meena: "Children are playing on the swings. Some birds are singing in the tall trees. A dog is running after a red ball on the green lawn." Which of the following is the BEST title for Meena's writing?

options.explanation: Classrooms do not typically have swings or large lawns.
The paragraph describes outdoor activities and birds singing, which suggests a pleasant day, not a rainy night.
Markets are for buying and selling, not for playing on swings.
The elements described (swings, trees, lawn, birds) are characteristic of a park.

questions.explanation: The details mention swings, tall trees, running on a green lawn, and birds singing, which clearly describe a scene at a park.
questions.hint: Look for keywords like 'swings', 'trees', and 'lawn' to identify the location.
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question: Read the incomplete descriptive sentence: "The garden was filled with ________ roses and ________ grass." Choose the pair of describing words (adjectives) that makes the sentence most meaningful:

options.explanation: Roses are commonly red, and grass is green, making this the most logical description.
Roses and grass are not typically described as loud or quiet.
Plants do not move, so they cannot be described as slow or fast.
While plants have weight, 'red' and 'green' are the primary visual descriptors for these specific items in a garden context.

questions.explanation: Describing words (adjectives) tell us about the appearance of nouns. Roses are typically described by colors like 'red' and grass by 'green'.
questions.hint: Think about the common colors associated with roses and grass.
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question: Assertion (A): We should give a clear title to our story or paragraph. Reason (R): A title helps the reader understand what the story or paragraph is mainly about. Which of the following is correct?

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.explanation: The reason a title is needed is precisely to give the reader an idea of the content.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
options.explanation: The reason provided is the direct explanation for the assertion.
The reason is factually true.
The assertion is also true; titles are essential.

questions.explanation: Giving a title is an essential part of creative writing because it prepares the reader and summarizes the main theme of the text. Both statements are true, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion.
questions.hint: Consider why a title is important for a reader before they start reading.
questions.subject: upbo4-english

questions.question: Amit received a wonderful storybook as a birthday gift from his uncle. He wants to write a short thank-you note to him. Which sentence should he include in the note?

options.text: Please grant me leave for two days.
options.explanation: This is for a leave application, not a thank-you note.

options.text: Thank you very much for the lovely gift.
options.explanation: This sentence directly expresses gratitude for the gift received.

options.text: You must come to my school tomorrow.
options.explanation: This is an invitation or command, not an expression of thanks.

options.text: I am writing to report a lost book.
options.explanation: This is for a lost and found report, not a thank-you note.

questions.explanation: A thank-you note is written to express appreciation and gratitude, so 'Thank you very much for the lovely gift' is the correct sentence to include.
questions.hint: What is the main purpose of a thank-you note?
questions.subject: upbo4-english
